message.content:
In a standard poker game the “highest number of hearts” a player can hold is simply limited by how many cards they’re dealt (plus any community cards that might be shared). Here’s a quick rundown:

| Game | Cards dealt to each player | Max hearts in a player’s hand | Max hearts a player can have *including community cards* |
|------|----------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| Texas Hold’em | 2 hole cards | 2 hearts | 7 hearts (2 hole + 5 board) |
| Five‑Card Draw | 5 cards | 5 hearts | 5 hearts (no community cards) |
| Seven‑Card Stud | 7 cards | 7 hearts | 7 hearts (no community cards) |
| Omaha | 4 hole cards | 4 hearts | 9 hearts (4 hole + 5 board) |

If you’re playing a single‑player variant (or just looking at the deck as a whole), the absolute theoretical maximum is 13 hearts – the entire hearts suit. But in any normal multi‑player game, the limit is the number of cards dealt to you (plus any community cards that might be shared).

So, in short: **the player who can have the most hearts is the one who receives the most cards**—in Texas Hold’em that’s 2 hearts in your hand (or 7 hearts total when you add the board).
